purpose: Rank disrupted roads or fixed mapped areas by the service restored at each recovery stage.

execution_tiers.name: Adaptive marginal service recovery
execution_tiers.condition: no more than 25 grounded actions; large networks use one fixed disclosed source cohort
execution_tiers.rule: Re-evaluate every remaining action after each restoration stage and choose the largest marginal harmonic-efficiency gain. Networks above 1200 nodes use the same deterministic 24-source cohort for every comparison.

execution_tiers.name: Large-candidate structural recovery screen
execution_tiers.rule: Rank once by disclosed weighted edge betweenness plus bridge increment; do not claim an uncomputed service-recovery curve.

execution_tiers.name: Gain per uploaded resource
execution_tiers.condition: complete positive repair cost or repair duration for every action
execution_tiers.rule: Divide the stage gain or structural score by the selected complete resource field.

mathematical_formulation.adaptive_gain: Delta(u | R_k) = E(G with R_k union {u} restored) - E(G with R_k restored)
mathematical_formulation.resource_score: Delta(u | R_k) / c_u or Delta(u | R_k) / tau_u
mathematical_formulation.area_action: One fixed 5 km mapped cell restores only its confirmed member roads as one screening action.

primary_sources.citation: Nurre et al. (2012), Restoring infrastructure systems

Maya Duque, P.A., Dolinskaya, I.S. and Sørensen, K. (2016). Network repair crew scheduling and routing for emergency relief distribution problem. European Journal of Operational Research, 248(1), 272-285.
Jenelius and Mattsson (2012), Road network vulnerability analysis of area-covering disruptions
Faturechi and Miller-Hooks (2014), Travel time resilience of roadway networks under disaster. Transportation Research Part B, 70, 47-64.

verification: Each action is restored at most once
Adaptive gains are recomputed after every stage
known_limitations: The adaptive sequence is greedy and does not claim a globally optimal multi-crew schedule.
The large-candidate tier is structural screening and withholds marginal service-recovery claims.
Operational scheduling requires crews, calendars, budgets, precedence and a declared service objective.
